title: A local immigration meaning case combines broad welcome with conditional inclusion
source_unit: adults surveyed in Chicago, suburban Cook County, and Lake County
geography: Chicago, suburban Cook County, and Lake County, Illinois, United States

observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate; reported weighting adjusted for gender, age, race/ethnicity, education, PUMA, and 2024 presidential vote.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±3.6 percentage points for the Chicago sample; nonresponse, mode, question wording, and subgroup limits remain.
observations.subgroup: Chicago adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: Support for a citizenship pathway does not imply support for every immigration level, admission rule, or local policy, and does not measure later political action.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; conditional citizenship pathway; suburban Cook County

denominator.unit: unweighted suburban Cook County survey respondents

favor_citizenship_path_for_undocumented_.unit: percent of suburban Cook County respondents

observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate; reported weighting adjusted for gender, age, race/ethnicity, education, PUMA, and 2024 presidential vote.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±3.6 percentage points for the suburban Cook County sample; nonresponse, mode, question wording, and subgroup limits remain.
observations.subgroup: Suburban Cook County adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower support relative to Chicago is a local descriptive difference, not evidence that suburban material conditions caused the policy view.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; conditional citizenship pathway; Lake County
observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate; reported weighting adjusted for gender, age, race/ethnicity, education, PUMA, and 2024 presidential vote.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±4.9 percentage points for the Lake County sample; the smaller sample is not used for fine-grained subgroup claims.
observations.subgroup: Lake County adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lake County support is not a county-wide causal estimate and cannot be inferred to the broader Chicago metropolitan area.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; Dreamer permanent legal status; Chicago
observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate from the same local survey; policy item is kept separate from the citizenship-path item.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±3.6 percentage points; support for one legal-status policy does not establish broader immigration approval or action.
observations.subgroup: Chicago adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: High support for Dreamer status can coexist with different views on immigration levels, border policy, admission criteria, and local service allocation.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; Dreamer permanent legal status; suburban Cook County

denominator.unit: unweighted suburban Cook County survey respondents

favor_dreamer_permanent_legal_status.unit: percent of suburban Cook County respondents

observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate from the same local survey; policy item is kept separate from the citizenship-path item.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±3.6 percentage points; this is a local attitude estimate, not a service, labor, housing, or political-action outcome.
observations.subgroup: Suburban Cook County adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: A majority policy response does not identify the material or cultural experience producing it, nor whether it translates into participation.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; Dreamer permanent legal status; Lake County
observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey estimate from the same local survey; policy item is kept separate from the citizenship-path item.
observations.uncertainty: Reported margin of error is ±4.9 percentage points; the smaller sample is not used for fine-grained partisan, race, or education claims.
observations.subgroup: Lake County adults surveyed in English or Spanish.
observations.counterinterpretation: Similar Dreamer-status support in suburban Cook and Lake County does not erase differences in rent, vacancy, population trajectory, language access, or health capacity.

boundary: This is a direct local-attitude case for three Illinois areas fielded April 13-23, 2026. It measures reported policy attitudes and legal-inclusion meaning, not observed political action, service use, labor outcomes, migration flows, or causal effects of local conditions. The ACS/CBP/HRSA context in the companion memo is not a respondent-level join, and the sample is not a national estimate. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.
